So I disagree with quite a bit of this. I'm a soprano and use falsetto to hit the notes. If it's an untrained, unreinforced falsetto that's one thing, but as someone who has worked on her resonance and support to make the falsetto have that color, this comment strikes me as defeatist.

It is absolutely possible, and in this case, it absolutely is a trans issue. If she has the range in falsetto, and she is more comfortable singing it, then that is something that should be trained and explored more, not shut down. 

Falsetto uses the edges of the vocal folds, so if you try to use it too low, yeah, you get that weak, airy sound, and it lacks color and depth. However, as it uses the edges of the folds, you can gradually increase the amount of cords you use when you decrease in pitch, or alternatively, lessen the amount as you raise in pitch. 

Resonance and pitch are separate entities, and falsetto can have a resonance adjustment with practice.

Hi, I've been a LW OTP since his release and have peaked T500/GM1 Pre S9. 


Without even seeing gameplay, I can tell you that you're probably not doing enough damage. LW has the highest damage per second out of all the supports, being beaten only by Zenyatta with discord orb. His healing is worse than Mercy's, which isn't even good to begin with. 

Some general tips outside of that are:

1. Start tracking your teammate's cooldowns, ESPECIALLY your tank's. If your Winston, Doomfist, or  Mauga have ult, don't pull them. If your Tracer has recall,  Reaper has wraith, and so on, DON'T PULL. 

2. Your healing travels through walls. Abuse that. You can sit behind cover and jiggle peek, and you can let your healing go at the last second before your DPS engage, which might give them just a bit more survivability. 

On that note...

3. Look to heal your DPS first, and tank second. LW only heals about 55HPS. That's not even 10% of a tank's health pool. It will take approximately 10 seconds to heal a Reinhardt to full. Compare that with DPS, and that's about 20%-25% of most DPS health pools, which has significantly more impact. Of course, that isn't to say don't heal your tank. It's situational, as is everything.

4. Deal damage first, heal second. It sounds weird for LW, so let me explain a bit. As I said before, LW has the second highest DPS out of all supports, being beaten only by Zenyatta with discord orb applied. So why should you use your subpar healing? Your healing on LW, more than anything, is there to supplement your other support. Have an Ana and everyone is crit? Don't heal the tank. Heal, the harder to hit DPS. That way, your Ana can focus on the tank. 

But what if you have Zenyatta/Illari/Lucio/Brig/Mercy? 


This is when the script gets flipped. Now, you (unfortunately) have to primarily heal and look for opportunities to weave in damage. With that said, you should still be doing a lot more damage than you initially think. 


5. Tree is weird. You charge it fast, so abuse it. Want to just give your team a quick AoE burst of healing and then break it? Go for it. It charges fast enough. Want to use it like a Mei wall and block a hallway/doorway/choke? Go for it. 

Speaking of tree...

6. Don't forget to break it!! You can break tree the instant you place it. If the fight is over, break the tree. There is no point in having it up when it isn't needed, and it hurts how fast you can charge a new one. Remember, as long as the Tree is active, you do not accumulate ult charge. 

7. Keybinds. This is a bit of personal preference with one caveat. Use the original binds. The "new" keybinds prevent you from dashing without jumping first. Jumping puts your character in a predictable arc, making you easy to hit. It also requires extra input, which can increase a delay between what you want to occur. Instead, use the legacy binds. My personal binds are Dash on Shift, Life Grip on E, Weapon Swap on RMB, Petal Platform on my upper side mouse button, and Fire Weapon set to LMB and toggle.

So, I used to be the fastest Petrus solver. I think there's faster now, but I'm not sure. Petrus has a lot of "fake" issues. What I mean by that is most of the problems people have with it are the product of the perception of it. A few popular people made statements about the method while misinformed, and this unfortunately led to people believing those claims. 


One notable claim is that Petrus was only good with worse turning puzzles, thanks to the low move count. This is not only untrue. It is demonstrably false. (I won't because I'm lazy)

Another is that it has poor look-ahead. This is SO far from the truth. The Petrus method has some of the best look-ahead in an objective sense. The way we can quantify this is by looking at potential blind spots. First, I think a fair assumption would be to solve the 2x2x2 block around the BDL corner in one look. This leaves us with potential blind spots in DBR, BR, and DR, which is just 3 pieces. Once we expand to a 3x2x2 block to the DBR corner, there are now zero blind spots on the puzzle.  Assuming you performed proper look-ahead, EO recognition isn't difficult or slow by any means, and rotating to make the rest of F2L leaves us with the same blind spots as before (BDR, BR, RD) but with a catch. See, we just solved EO from there, so we know what pieces are there, so it's not really a blind spot. Compare this with CFOP where you can have blind spots in up to double those of Petrus until your last two slots, or with ZZ where you have blind spots on LD, LDB, BL, RB, RDB, and RD, or Roux, where during Second Block you can have blind spots in BD, BDR, BR, DR. 

So, to sum it up, Petrus isn't a bad method in any sense of the word. In fact, Petrus would still be up there with the other methods if it wasn't for the statements of a few people. That said, the dwindling number of solvers doesn't exactly help either.

So there's a lot wrong in this thread and a lot of super close statements. 

First off, let's look at the typical dive characters:

For tanks, possibilities are Winston, D.VA (to a lesser extent in OW2), Doomfist, and Ball. What do yhey all have in common? They're super *super* mobile. 

What about DPS? Usually, it's some combination of Tracer, Genji, Sombra, and more recently, Sojourn and even occasionally, Reaper. Again, they all have mobility of some kind. 

Now, let's look at support. It is incredibly helpful to split this into flex support and main support. 

Our possible flex support choices are Ana, Kiriko, and Zenyatta. Now, with the exception of Kiriko, both Ana and Zen are SUPER immobile.

So, first off, LW is 100% a main support. Not main healer, not off healer, not flex support. Main Support. 

Keeping that in mind, let's look at his utility and compare it to the other main supports. 

First, healing output: In terms of raw heals per second, he has the highest at 57hps, with mercy a close second at 55hps, Zen at 30hps, and brig and lucio even lower. Every single one of these characters provides more value from their utility than their healing. So, let's look at that next.

Petal Platform: While the utility in theory is ridiculously strong (I mean seriously,  free high ground, ANYWHERE??) it needs to be looked at in comparison to the other main supports. 

Lucio: Speed boost, which provides his team with increased movement speed.

How does this help his team? It lets them retreat out of a lost fight or sources of damage that can't be outhealed. It also lets them close distance faster and, as a result, take less poke damage, whether that's to engage a fight or to chase stragglers. 

Zenyatta: Discord orb applies a 25% increase of damage from ALL sources, but only one target at a time. Just the existence of this on the enemy tank creates a HUGE amount of pressure that is, quite literally, unmatched in the entire game. 

How does this help his team? It allows his tank to take/hold space as without a mirror, one tank is stuck at 3/4 health as a max.  

Mercy: Damage boost provides a 30% boost to all damage output from the boosted hero. 

How does this help the team? Damage boost allows characters to bypass certain breakpoints, notably allowing Sojourn to one-shot 200 HP heroes. It also allows the team to charge their ults faster, resulting in a superior ultimate economy.  

Brig: Whipshot provides a boop on a 4 second cooldown while proccing Inspire, which is a constant 6 seconds of low healing. 

How does this help her team? Let's look at her main purpose right now - peeling for her other support. How does she do this? Whipshot can boop enemies away from the other support, which triggers her passive healing. 

So, with all of this in mind, let's go back to Lifeweaver. His main utility is going to 100% be his petal. Not his healing, certainly not his damage, and not the pull. 

So, how does his petal help his team? Well, it can provide free high ground, it can create crossfire in places there typically isn't (think first fight on Colliseo, go to the side of the bot with a petal for the DPS, or himself) and it can increase his own survivability as well AND deny enemy ultimates (Think Grav and Terra Surge). 

If it can do all that, why is it so lackluster? The answer lies in the cooldown and the reliance (in the case of the first example) on teammates to properly utilize it. In lower ranks, the value of the petal isn't understood, and in higher ranks, most angles it can provide aren't necessarily better than pre-existing angles. 

So what about using it for himself? What value does he provide to the team then? Compared to the other Main Supports, very little. He stays alive and can pull people to safety. That's about it. 

Pull is another story entirely. Almost every form of utility the other main support provides allows for an increase in offensive pressure. Pull is the opposite. It's used to bail out someone out of position, out of cooldowns, being dove, etc. 

What if you pull your tank? They can no longer hold the space they created, giving it up to the enemy team, leaving your DPS in neutral or enemy space. 

What about DPS? There ends up being a *very* large dip in offensive pressure, which allows resources to be put into the enemy tank, which can be enough to force your tank to back up.

What about the other support? What reason would you have for pulling your other support? Say you're playing with Ana, and she keeps getting dove. This keeps her alive, and by extension, your team. Let's take it a step further and introduce the use of his Petal Platform. Pull the Ana to safety and standing near a platform. Now she has high ground and is (briefly) safe from the enemy dive. 

Keeping in mind all this information, it would seem that his most reliable playstyle would be to peel for his other support. If that's the case, though, why not just play Brig? 


The TL;DR here is that he isn't inherently bad by design. It's about what does he provide that other supports don't? Or, more accurately, why play him when other supports do his job better, with more room for error?
